beats.label: hook
beats.narration: Topping off the same tire every week? That's a leak.
beats.visual: Extreme macro on a rubber tire valve stem where it meets the alloy wheel, a single soap bubble swelling outward from the base of the stem and quivering in cold morning light, shallow depth of field, dark wet pavement bokeh behind.
beats.motion: Slow continuous macro push-in; the bubble grows, trembles, and holds without popping.
beats.audioCue: Low ambient hiss of escaping air, no music sting.
beats.safeZoneNotes: Bubble center-frame; keep top 12% / bottom 20% clear for IG UI.

beats.label: symptom
beats.narration: Losing a pound a month is normal. Weekly top-offs can point to a leak.
beats.visual: Tight low-angle three-quarter view of a single tire's contact patch bulging visibly flatter against the pavement, the tire behind it sitting taut and round in soft background blur, faint frost on the asphalt, early flat daylight.
beats.motion: Slow creeping dolly that settles on the soft tire's contact patch, shallow focus throughout.
beats.safeZoneNotes: Contact patch center-frame, pavement horizon low.

beats.label: explanation
beats.narration: Usually it's a nail, a cracked valve stem, or corrosion at the rim.
beats.visual: Three objects isolated on a clean dark field: a roofing nail sunk into a block of tread rubber, a split and perished rubber valve stem, and a pale crust of corrosion along the bead seat where rubber meets alloy.
beats.motion: The frame glides between the three objects in turn, each rotating slowly on its own axis.
beats.audioCue: Soft mechanical tick as the frame settles on each object.
beats.safeZoneNotes: Objects held to the middle band of frame.

beats.label: proof_demo
beats.narration: Soapy water finds all three — bubbles mark the spot. Do not guess.
beats.visual: A film of soapy water clinging across a tire's bead seat and valve stem, a cluster of bubbles inflating outward from one single spot as escaping air pushes through the film.
beats.motion: Macro push-in on the bubble cluster as it swells and multiplies at the leak point.

beats.label: branded_cta
beats.narration: Where it bubbles decides the fix.
beats.visual: The same valve stem and bead seat, soap film gone, rubber still and dry, warm late-afternoon shop light raking across it, matching the opening angle.
beats.motion: Camera settles into a still hold on the opening framing for a seamless loop.
beats.safeZoneNotes: End-card overlay composited in post, bottom-safe.

loopIdea: The closing beat holds the same valve stem and bead seat beat 1 opened on, soap film gone and the rubber dry at the identical raking angle, so a replay reads as the next bubble swelling from that same spot.
voiceoverScript: Topping off that tire every week? A pound a month is normal, but weekly can point to a leak. Usually a nail, a cracked valve stem, or rim corrosion. Soapy water finds all three - bubbles mark the spot.
selectedCaption: Topping off the same tire every week? That's not the weather — that's a leak. A healthy tire loses about a pound a month, not a pound a week. Soapy water on the tread, the valve stem, and the rim edge will bubble right where the air is escaping. Where it bubbles decides the fix, so do not guess. Nick's Tire & Auto, 17625 Euclid Ave, Cleveland - (216) 862-0005
